lines.text: A string thirty-six units long. How many different triangles can you bend it into?
lines.caption: A string thirty-six units long. How many different triangles can you bend it into?

lines.text: Whole-number sides, all three different. Most kids lose count!
lines.caption: Whole-number sides, all three different. Most kids lose count!

lines.text: Whole-number sides, all three different, and a perimeter of thirty-six.
lines.caption: Whole-number sides, all three different, and a perimeter of thirty-six.

lines.text: The trick: fix the longest side. It has to be from twelve to seventeen.
lines.caption: The trick: fix the longest side. It has to be from twelve to seventeen.

lines.text: A longest side of seventeen gives seven triangles. Sixteen gives five. Fifteen, four.
lines.caption: A longest side of seventeen gives seven triangles. Sixteen gives five. Fifteen, four.

lines.text: Fourteen gives two, thirteen gives one, and twelve gives none.
lines.caption: Fourteen gives two, thirteen gives one, and twelve gives none.

lines.text: Seven plus five plus four plus two plus one: nineteen!
lines.caption: Seven plus five plus four plus two plus one: nineteen!

lines.text: An organized list never loses a triangle.
lines.caption: An organized list never loses a triangle.

lines.text: Want to see why? The full lesson has two neat ways and every trap.
